verses.text: Then the people of the land took Jehoahaz the son of Josiah, and made him king in his father’s place in Jerusalem.
Joahaz was twenty-three years old when he began to reign; and he reigned three months in Jerusalem.
The king of Egypt removed him from office at Jerusalem, and fined the land one hundred talents of silver and a talent  of gold.
The king of Egypt made Eliakim his brother king over Judah and Jerusalem, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. Neco took Joahaz his brother, and carried him to Egypt.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. He did that which was evil in Yahweh his God’s sight.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against him, and bound him in fetters to carry him to Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar also carried some of the vessels of Yahweh’s house to Babylon, and put them in his temple at Babylon.

Now the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, and his abominations which he did, and that which was found in him, behold, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah; and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place.
Jehoiachin was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem. He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight.
At the return of the year, king Nebuchadnezzar sent and brought him to Babylon, with the valuable vessels of Yahweh’s house, and made Zedekiah his brother king over Judah and Jerusalem.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.
He did that which was evil in Yahweh his God’s sight. He didn’t humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet speaking from Yahweh’s mouth.
He also rebelled against king Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God; but he stiffened his neck, and hardened his heart against turning to Yahweh, the God of Israel.
Moreover all the chiefs of the priests, and the people, trespassed very greatly after all the abominations of the nations; and they polluted Yahweh’s house which he had made holy in Jerusalem.
Yahweh, the God of their fathers, sent to them by his messengers, rising up early and sending, because he had compassion on his people, and on his dwelling place;
but they mocked the messengers of God, and despised his words, and scoffed at his prophets, until Yahweh’s wrath arose against his people, until there was no remedy.

Therefore he brought on them the king of the Chaldeans, who killed their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary, and had no compassion on young man or virgin, old man or gray-headed. He gave them all into his hand.
All the vessels of God’s house, great and small, and the treasures of Yahweh’s house, and the treasures of the king, and of his princes, all these he brought to Babylon.
They burned God’s house, and broke down the wall of Jerusalem, and burned all its palaces with fire, and destroyed all of its valuable vessels.
He carried those who had escaped from the sword away to Babylon, and they were servants to him and his sons until the reign of the kingdom of Persia,
to fulfill Yahweh’s word by Jeremiah’s mouth, until the land had enjoyed its Sabbaths. As long as it lay desolate, it kept Sabbath, to fulfill seventy years.

Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that Yahweh’s word by the mouth of Jeremiah might be accomplished, Yahweh stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, so that he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and put it also in writing, saying,

“Thus says Cyrus king of Persia, ‘Yahweh, the God of heaven, has given all the kingdoms of the earth to me; and he has commanded me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Whoever there is among you of all his people, Yahweh his God be with him, and let him go up.’”

footnotes.content: The land took Josiah's son and made him king—but notice what the next verses will show: the people had wandered so far from seeking the Lord that their choice of a king couldn't save them. Sometimes we think a good leader will fix everything, but the healing must start in our own hearts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Twenty-three years old, three months on the throne—Jehoahaz had barely time to learn his own name as king before the world changed for him. How quickly kingdoms rise and fall when they're not built on the Rock.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The king of Egypt removed him—Egypt, the ancient power to the south, had come north to reshape Judah's throne. Egypt stands in Scripture as the type of worldly power; when we look to the world instead of the Lord, we'll find ourselves paying tribute rather than tribute.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A name changed, a brother carried away to captivity—Eliakim becomes Jehoiakim, remade by foreign hands. But the Lord's renaming—that happens from the inside, when His Spirit rewrites who we are.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He did evil in the sight of the Lord—and we see the age-old pattern: the king's heart turns from Yahweh, and the whole kingdom follows. Evil doesn't whisper quietly; it leads loud, and the people hear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bound in fetters, carried to Babylon—the king's chains are the kingdom's chains. Nebuchadnezzar's hand is real, but read it this way: the hand of God was moving through history, allowing judgment to come.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The vessels of the house of the Lord carried to Babylon—the sacred things taken to a foreign temple. Yet even this cup of humiliation Judah had to drink prepared the way for something the Lord knew was coming: restoration.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The rest of Jehoiakim's acts are written in the book of the kings—what a thin memorial to a life that turned from the Lord. Our deeds, however grand they seem, are seen by Him; the only deeds worth remembering are the ones done from a heart that loved Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eight years old, three months and ten days—a child placed on a throne in a kingdom already unraveling. Even a child innocent of his father's sins inherits a house divided. How grateful I am that our Father offers us a clean start through His Son.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: At the return of the year, Nebuchadnezzar brought him to Babylon—the machinery of judgment turns at the Lord's pace, not our haste. Even the heathen king moves according to a script written before time began.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zedekiah, twenty-one years old, reigned eleven years—the last king of Judah before the exile, a man caught in a time when choices had narrowed to almost nothing. Yet even then, a choice remained: to humble himself before the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He didn't humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet—stubborn where he should have been wise. The prophet stood before him with the word of the Lord, and Zedekiah turned his face away. How many messages from the Lord do we dismiss because they don't suit our plans?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He stiffened his neck and hardened his heart—a long road to that moment, but notice: the hardening is deliberate, not a thing that happened to him. We can turn toward the Lord or turn away; each turn makes the next one easier or harder.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All the chiefs of the priests and the people trespassed greatly—priests first named, then the people following. When the shepherds go astray, the flock scatters. The holiness the Lord had made in that place was theirs to guard, and they gave it away.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rising up early and sending his messengers—the phrase echoes Genesis and the patience of a God who kept sending, kept calling. Even here, at the brink of judgment, He shows us His compassion. He didn't want to bring calamity; He wanted them to come home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They mocked, despised, and scoffed—the path to judgment is paved with refusals. The Lord's wrath rose because He had been refused, again and again, by people who knew better. Sometimes judgment is simply the end of patience, not the beginning of cruelty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He had no compassion on young man or virgin, old man or gray-headed—Nebuchadnezzar's sword did not spare, but behind that sword was the hand that allowed it. The conquered see cruelty; the Lord sees a people receiving the wages of turning away from Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All the vessels of God's house, great and small—they stripped the sanctuary bare. What had been set apart for holy use was now plunder, belonging to foreign gods in a foreign place. When we turn from the Lord, everything we held sacred becomes only a thing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They burned God's house and broke down the wall—the temple, the city, the palace all fallen in flames. It's a sight that looks like the end of the world to those who watch it happen. And yet, the Lord had already seen past it to restoration.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They were servants to him and his sons until the reign of Persia—exile, captivity, and the slow passage of years in a strange land. But notice the word 'until'; there was always an end written into this trial, known to the Lord before it began.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The land kept Sabbath, fulfilling seventy years—even in emptiness and desolation, the Lord's purposes moved forward. The land itself rested as it should have when Israel would not obey. What a tender mercy, woven even through judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh stirred up the spirit of Cyrus—a pagan king, unaware of why his heart inclined toward rebuilding a foreign temple. Yet the Lord moves the hearts of men like chess pieces on a board He sees from the beginning. Our restoration often comes through hands we'd never expect.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo of this: the God of heaven gave all kingdoms into His hand, yet He commands us—free to go, free to build, free to return to Him. Looking back from 2026, we see how the Lord still stirs hearts toward rebuilding what was broken, and still calls us to come home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
